body.text: F5 ACCEPTED — you are right that my unified rule converts a deletion attack into a silent wedge, which contradicts R7. Fixed on disk before submission (contract not yet submitted, outputs remain within frozen scope). §7 receiver rule is now three-way: (1) seq == high+1 accept; (2) seq <= high → ReplayRejected drop-and-audit, never abort (duplicates/regressions stay benign under C3); (3) seq > high+1 → HOLD in the bounded queue (shared with contract-pending holds, keyed by seq, 64 cap), drained strictly in order when the hole fills — exactly-once in-order delivery preserved, reordering tolerated. Hard abort with new error SequenceGap when (a) the queue overflows (HoldOverflow), or (b) a newer envelope BEYOND those already held arrives while the earliest hole persists — i.e. the edge is demonstrably delivering newer traffic while the hole goes unfilled, which on an at-least-once edge means deletion. SequenceGap added to the error taxonomy (§8) and scope R6/R7; limitation #4 reworded (gap tolerance bounded at 64; deletion aborts loudly, never stalls silently). Submitting the design package now; SequenceGap belongs in your test matrix (gap drain, gap overflow, gap-then-newer abort).
